# Feature: Raft block — sanity check

<!-- Generated by the project-manager tool from pm.yml. Do not edit by hand; the store is the source of truth. -->

## Goal

Sanity-check candidate mechanic #86 (Raft block) from Blocks before it is used in real levels. Effect: Ride across water, sinks after 10 tiles travelled. Unique: a vehicle with a 10-tile lifespan shown in the conditional slot under the inventory. Useful: crosses water with a distance budget, not just a key slot. Source status in the candidate file is 'revised'; it was revised from human review and is now treated as a trial candidate.

## User Story

**As a** player

**I want** ride across water, sinks after 10 tiles travelled.

**So that** crosses water with a distance budget, not just a key slot.

## High-Level Use Case

The player meets Raft block for the first time in its teaching room (mech-86-raft-block-room). Teaching moment: First room: a twelve-tile water crossing with a banked island at eight tiles. A player who rides straight for the far bank sinks two tiles short and respawns at the checkpoint, which teaches that the raft's ten tiles are a budget to be spent between banks. The sanity check plays that room, exercises every rule below, and records a replayable session.

## Player-Facing Behavior

- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Step onto the raft from a bank and each move travels one water tile with you aboard, shallow or deep
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Stepping onto a bank ends the ride
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: It cannot enter floor, void, fire or lava; a bank is the only way off
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: After 10 tiles travelled it sinks and you respawn at your checkpoint
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: A remaining-tiles counter appears in a conditional GUI slot under the inventory while you ride

## Edge Cases & Rules

- It cannot enter floor, void, fire or lava; a bank is the only way off
- Movement/state stays deterministic: state advances only through the pure step function with recorded t_ms; a recorded session replays to the same end state.
- Restart (R / restart) restores the room to its initial state, including this mechanic.

## UI / Feedback

- The player sees Raft block's effect happen on its tile(s) exactly as the rules above describe; no hidden state.
- Any counter, inventory or HUD impact follows the rules above; if a rule needs a counter it is shown while it matters (see Open Questions).
- Failure in the teaching room returns the player to the room start / checkpoint for an immediate retry.

## Assets & Level Data Needed

- Level JSON: new Test Level mech-86-raft-block-room (rows + legend) implementing the teaching moment above.
- Sprites/defs: reuse existing tiles where the mechanic reuses an existing tile; add a new sprite/tile def only if this mechanic introduces a new tile (confirm in the implement task).
- Source: plans/level-design/candidate-mechanics/blocks.yml mechanic #86.

## Open Questions

- Human review to honour: I think to make this more interesting is that the Raft has limited use.
- Human review to honour: So I think maybe has a life span of lets say 10 blocks.
- Human review to honour: We would need a GUI conter to show this. I think having a conditional spot GUI for elements under inventory is not a bad idea.
- Synergies deferred to a later run (do not build now): Deep water (41): the raft crosses deep water without the slow wading cost, but the 10-tile budget still binds.
- Demos deferred (reference only): Current tile (42): current does not move a raft, so it is the controlled alternative to drifting.
- Confirm any new sprite/tile def and any HUD counter this mechanic needs before the implement task is approved.
